claims.text: An FCC-matrix high-entropy alloy can contain L12-ordered precipitates.
Introducing 5–10 vol% coherent, Ti-rich L12 precipitates into an FCC Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix is feasible.
Ni3Ti or Fe3Ti can serve as the proposed coherent L12-ordered precipitate phase.
The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy is a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy.
High symmetry and itinerant-electron behavior suppress orbital magnetic moments in the initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy.
The initial alloy has coercivity below 50 Oe.
Solution treatment followed by aging at 500–700 °C will nucleate and grow coherent Ti-rich L12 precipitates while preserving the FCC matrix.
Aging for 10–50 hours will produce precipitates 5–20 nm in size.
A precipitate size of 5–20 nm is optimal for magnetic domain-wall pinning in this alloy.
Composition can be tuned so that the FCC matrix remains ferromagnetic with a Curie temperature above 400 K.
Coherent L12 precipitates act as magnetic domain-wall pinning centers.
Strain around coherent precipitates locally breaks cubic symmetry and enhances spin-orbit coupling and orbital moment at the precipitate-matrix interface.
Precipitate strain distorts the electronic band structure and lifts d-orbital degeneracy.
Precipitate-matrix interfaces increase the energy barrier for domain-wall motion and thereby increase coercivity.
The aged alloy will have room-temperature coercivity above 100 Oe.
The aged alloy will have a higher orbital-to-spin magnetic moment ratio than the single-phase state.
The aged alloy will retain a Curie temperature above 350 K.
Composition and annealing temperature can control decomposition length scale and formation of B2 plus BCC phases in a high-entropy alloy.
Phase decomposition in high-entropy alloys is driven by enthalpy of mixing.
Incoherent, non-magnetic, antiferromagnetic, sigma, or Laves secondary phases would degrade the target magnetic properties.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies only when precipitates remain coherent, whereas the falsification rule treats observation of incoherent precipitates as falsification. Incoherence would instead show failure to realize the specified intervention or a violation of the hypothesis's applicability condition.
